# CrossArm

> CrossArm converts ABB industrial robot programs written in RAPID into FANUC TP programs (.LS). It reads a complete RobotWare backup (every robot task, EIO.cfg, system modules) or loose .mod/.modx/.sys files and writes one FANUC program per routine, plus an HTML report of everything that still needs a person. Offline; Windows executable or Python 3.11+ with no runtime dependency. Licence: Business Source License 1.1 (free for evaluation and other non-production use).

Key facts:

- Converts: MoveJ/MoveL/MoveC/MoveAbsJ with their targets (including Offs and RelTool), robtarget quaternion to W,P,R, ABB confdata to FANUC CONFIG, tool and work objects to UTOOL/UFRAME, speed and zone data, num/bool/byte data to R[]/F[], data of RECORD types field by field (each field a program changes a register or a flag named by its path, the others written as their value, a speed or zone set once as a constant), strings the programs change to SR[] (texts loaded by a CA_TEXT program CrossArm writes, compared with IF SR[a]=SR[b],JMP, StrLen/StrPart/StrMatch/NumToStr as STRLEN/SUBSTR/FINDSTR/SR=R, a comparison where texts could differ by case alone left TODO), digital, group and analog I/O typed by EIO.cfg, PulseDO, InvertDO, clocks to TIMER, IF/ELSEIF/FOR/WHILE, TEST/CASE to SELECT, conditions calling the backup's own bool functions (written as the test they make), calls with num/bool/string/robtarget/record/tooldata/wobjdata/speeddata/zonedata/switch arguments (a routine given its speed and zone makes its moves with them from registers, L P[1] R[1]mm/sec CNT R[3], the call passing the mm/s, the joint % and the CNT of each corner, fine as FINE; points in position registers, frames as their numbers selected with UTOOL_NUM=AR[n], records as their components, nums passed by reference read back after the call), Incr/Decr/Add/Clear, RAPID math functions (Pow, Sqrt, Sin...) of data no program changes worked out at conversion time, a WaitTime of a calculation as WAIT R[n], RelTool of a point given at run time as Tool_Offset, calculations of several operations (one per line in scratch registers), points worked out at run time (palletizing Offs of loop counters, RelTool, CRobT; CRobT without \Tool and \WObj as PR[k]=LPOS in the frames selected) in position registers, arrays of points and numbers indexed at run time (PR[R[n]], R[R[n]]) (CALL NAME(args) / AR[n]), calls to the integrator's own move routines, interrupts (ISignalDI, ISignalDO, IPers) as FANUC condition monitors (MONITOR / WHEN ... CALL TRAP, a relay per interrupt for a shared TRAP and INTNO), waits with MaxTime and their ERROR handler's timeout path, TPWrite to MESSAGE. SETUP_FRAMES.LS sets the tool and user frames on the robot.
- Reports as TODO rather than guessing: other parameter types, FUNC doing more than return a test, timer interrupts and a TRAP that moves the robot, frames and targets computed from data that changes at run time (frames computed from fixed values are worked out at conversion time), error handlers beyond wait timeouts, string and point fields of records, StrToVal/StrFind/StrMemb, arrays of records, GOTO, late binding, ABB-specific instructions. Two causes of their own: a routine or data the backup does not declare ("routine or data not in the backup", saying what to add), and what TP has nothing for ("RAPID instruction without a TP equivalent": files, sockets, byte buffers, operator dialogs, positions read on the robot, also through a routine of the backup that uses them, with the chain). The report gives the share of the RAPID instructions converted, by area.
- Measured, not assumed: the arm-configuration and joint-axis conventions of both makers were measured with RobotStudio and ROBOGUIDE; generated programs were loaded in ROBOGUIDE and matched its re-export byte for byte; on 16 test moves (rotated tools and work objects, Offs, RelTool) the flange pose computed by RobotStudio and the one reached by ROBOGUIDE running the converted program agree within 0.004 mm and 0.001 degree. Speeds and zones are measured on both robots (RobotStudio and ROBOGUIDE): joint % = RAPID speed / 4500 mm/s, and each zone is written as the CNT that rounds a corner as much at the move's speed; converted moves take within 20 % of the ABB's time and round corners to within 0.8 mm.
- Writes (version 1.7.0): one .LS per routine, SETUP_FRAMES.LS, crossarm_mapping.json, crossarm_points.json (every point written and the RAPID it came from), and crossarm_report.html, an interactive offline page that opens on an analysis (a decision, ready / workable / not ready, by a fixed rule printed under it: workable from 85 % of the RAPID instructions converted and at most 3 blocking causes; the 3 to 7 things to do first; the main TODO causes; the share converted by area; controller resources near their limit), then each RAPID routine and its TP side by side, TODO lines marked by cause, the items to review filtered or searched, and a commissioning checklist (frames, tools, payloads, I/O, registers, points to touch up, motion to check) whose ticks are kept in the browser. With --tp / --tp-robot ROBOT (a ROBOGUIDE robot folder or a Setrobot robot.ini), FANUC MakeTP, installed with ROBOGUIDE, also makes binary .TP programs in a TP folder, for a controller without the ASCII Upload option. A jointtarget read on the robot (CJointT) is kept in a joint position register (PR[k]=JPOS), its axes read with the measured conventions.
- Programs the integrator provides: the mapping key external_routines ({"WriteLog": {"program": "WRITE_LOG"}}) names a TP or KAREL program written on the FANUC side in place of a routine CrossArm cannot write (not in the backup, or using files, sockets or byte buffers): its calls become CALL WRITE_LOG(args), the routine is not written, and the report and checklist list each program to provide with its arguments (AR[n]) and the num read back. The mapping file CrossArm writes lists the candidates with "program": null, inactive until filled in. Measured on ROBOGUIDE.
- KAREL for what TP cannot compute (option --karel, off by default; step 6 of the window): poses computed at run time (PoseMult, PoseInv, RelTool, DefFrame of poses kept in position registers), the tool and user frames calibrated from them (UFRAME[n]=PR[k], UTOOL[n]=PR[k]) and RAPID's text files (Open, Write, Close, written on the controller's UD1: byte for byte as RAPID writes them) become CALL CA_POSEMULT(a,b,c), CA_POSEINV, CA_RELTOOL, CA_DEFFRAME, CA_FILE: CrossArm's own KAREL programs, written in a KAREL folder of the output and compiled to .pc by FANUC ktrans when it is installed (with ROBOGUIDE), else delivered as .kl with the command. A real robot needs the KAREL option (R632); load the .pc before the .LS. Sockets stay TODO (KAREL socket messaging needs client tags configured on the robot). Without --karel the output is unchanged and the report says how many TODO it would convert. Measured on ROBOGUIDE.
- Converting again keeps the touch-ups: crossarm convert --keep-taught PATH (repeatable) reads the robot's programs as they are now (.LS, or .TP decoded by FANUC PrintTP) and the crossarm_points.json of the earlier conversion; a point touched up on the robot keeps its taught value unless its ABB position or frames changed (then theoretical again, listed to touch up again with how far the touch-up was). Statuses: kept, touch up again, theoretical, new, gone, not read. A conversion made before 1.6 has no crossarm_points.json: convert the old backup again once. Measured on ROBOGUIDE.
- Numbering fits the target cell: given the FANUC robot's own backup, CrossArm leaves its frame, register and I/O numbers and its program names free; a mapping file pins any number.
- Output is a starting point for commissioning: payloads, reachability and every TODO must be checked before running a robot, and the points touched up: they are the ABB's, as theoretical points. CrossArm aims for a path within 10 mm of the ABB's; measured against an IRB 6700 on two FANUC robots, within 4 mm (approaches, retracts, corners, reversals, zigzags).
